chunks: Al-‘Alā’ narrated from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about a man who purchased a bondwoman, and her owner had not been having relations with her. Should he still observe istibrā’ for her womb? He said: "Yes."

I said: "A bondwoman who has not menstruated—what should he do with her?" He said: "Her case is serious. If he goes to her, then he must not ejaculate until it becomes clear to him whether she is pregnant or not."
I said to him: "In how long will that become clear to him?" He said: "In forty-five nights."

key_terms.جَارِيَةً: a bondwoman or female slave being discussed in the legal ruling
key_terms.خَمْسٍ وَ أَرْبَعِينَ لَيْلَةً: forty-five nights, the period mentioned for clarity regarding pregnancy
key_terms.رَحِمَهَا: her womb, the subject of the legal precaution
key_terms.لَمْ تَحِضْ: she has not menstruated, describing the special case in question
key_terms.يَسْتَبْرِئُ: to observe istibrā’, meaning to ensure the womb is free from pregnancy

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on istibrā’ for a purchased bondwoman, especially if she has not menstruated?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on istibrā’ for a purchased bondwoman, affirming that her womb must be checked even if the previous owner was not having relations with her. It also addresses the more difficult case of one who has not menstruated, stating that pregnancy should be clarified, with a period of forty-five nights mentioned for this determination.
